last_reply:
I'll start by looking at what's actually in this workspace and the evidence captured.The dashboard is now a working dashboard, not a picture of one. Every card, chart, the app ranking and the analytics recompute from fresh samples every second, the Apps screen lists all 265 processes with a filter, sorting and per-row memory/process detail, the Analytics screen calculates its averages, peaks and findings for whichever time range you pick, and the charts zoom on drag, reset on double-click, show a graph when you hover a value, and the gear lets you choose which cards are shown. It can also be pointed at your real syswatch agent: the gear's collector box asks `/api/current` and friends, and if nothing answers it keeps sampling by itself instead of failing.

Two things differ on purpose. The cards hold the last recorded second for about twenty seconds (or until you pick a screen or a range, which starts it at once) because the reference's opened menus quote exact numbers from a different second than its screenshot — 46.4 % versus 39.0 %, 571 MB versus 477 MB — so those four numbers can't all match; everything else measures at 97–98 % like the original, same page heights at all three widths. And the app list now shows real percentages and proportional bars where your collector's payload returned 0.0 % for every process, which is exactly the dead look you complained about.

What's left for you to decide: whether the page should stay wired to your running agent at 127.0.0.1:8123 (its server would need to allow requests from the page's address), or whether the twenty-second settle before the numbers move is too long for your taste.
